chunks: 5. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadalah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from al-Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Throne encompasses the heavens and the heavens and the earth.' Are the heavens and the earth greater than the Throne, or is the Throne greater than the heavens and the earth? He answered, 'Indeed, everything is in the Throne.' Chapter: The Fitrah of Allah, the Mighty and High, creating upon Tawhid.

key_terms.الْكُرْسِيُّ: The Throne or Seat of Divine Authority

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the relationship between the Throne and the heavens and earth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the apparent paradox in Surah Al-A'raf 7:156 by asserting that the Kursi (Throne/Seat of Divine Knowledge) encompasses all creation, thereby affirming that God's knowledge and power are not limited by spatial dimensions. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on Tawhid, distinguishing between the Creator's infinite attribute and the created universe's finitude. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how divine omnipresence coexists with the physical order of the cosmos.
